fr.elements: Main Residence; Access Drive; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Long Driveway; Open Terrain; Limited Turnaround Space
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance, visible from both directions on the road.
• Mark the driveway entrance with tall reflective posts so it can be located quickly at night or in smoke.
• Keep the full width of the driveway clear of overgrown vegetation on both sides to allow large emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Trim tree branches along the driveway to a minimum height that allows fire apparatus and ambulances to pass without stopping.
• Create a turnaround area near the residence large enough for a fire engine or ambulance to reverse direction without backing the full length of the driveway.
• Mark any turnaround area with visible indicators so arriving responders can locate it without searching.
• Keep the turnaround area clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and stored materials at all times.
• Clear a staging area near the residence where responders can park and work without blocking the driveway for other arriving units.
• Maintain a gap in dense vegetation on at least one side of the residence so responders can move around the building on foot.
• Notify your local fire station of the single-access driveway and long approach distance so they can note it in their dispatch records before an emergency occurs.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Open Terrain; Long Driveway; Single Access Route; Grass Cover; Scattered Shrubs; Open Green Space; Brush Area; Limited Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs that are growing directly against the walls and foundation of the structure.
• Thin trees closest to the structure to increase open space between the canopy and the building.
• Remove brush from the areas immediately surrounding the structure on all sides.
• Clear grass from the ground directly around the structure, especially where it contacts the foundation or siding.
• Separate shrub clusters near the structure so there are visible gaps of bare ground between them.
• Thin the brush areas nearest to the structure to reduce the amount of continuous plant material leading toward it.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches along its full length.
• Remove shrubs and tall grass growing along the edges of the driveway that could block vehicle passage or line-of-sight.
• Keep a clear, unobstructed travel lane along the full length of the driveway for emergency vehicle access.
• Cut grass on the open terrain close to the structure down to a short height before dry conditions arrive.
• Remove dead or dry plant material from the brush areas nearest to the structure.
• Create visible open ground between shrub groups and the structure on all sides.
• Keep vegetation along the single access route trimmed back so the roadway edge is clearly visible and passable.
